issue.title: Repo stats and incoming-commit counts still include merge commits, disagreeing with the default merge-hidden commit log
issue.description: Epic sase-i8 made merge commits first-class in the VCS commit log -- hidden by default, revealable with MergeVisibility -- but two commit-counting surfaces were never threaded through that policy, so they now disagree with the default timeline once a repo's history stops being squash-only. Verified on master today: (1) src/sase/vcs_provider/plugins/_git_query_ops.py vcs_repo_stats runs 'git rev-list --count HEAD' (line 307) and 'git shortlog -sne HEAD' (line 313) with no --no-merges and no MergeVisibility parameter, even though the same file already has _merge_visibility_args and threads merges through the ahead/behind and log paths; (2) src/sase/updates/incoming_commits.py _fetch_git_incoming_commits counts a revision range with plain 'git rev-list --count' (line 268) and lists it with plain 'git log', exposing no MergeVisibility choice. On this repo the gap is 101 merge commits out of 12100, so repo stats and incoming-update totals overcount by ~1% and contributor attribution includes merge authors. Both were routed onto epic sase-i8 as DISCOVERED ISSUE notes by sase-i8.10.land instead of standalone tasks; that epic was closed 2026-08-11, so they are filed here together because they share one remediation. SCOPE: give both surfaces a MergeVisibility parameter defaulting to the same hide policy as the commit log, with tests against real merge history.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-i8.10.4 — closed phase whose land triage first proposed both surfaces; its notes on closed epic sase-i8 hold the original wording.
